mcqs.q: What did this Portuguese study conclude about empathy as a cause of pet relinquishment?
o: Low empathy is the primary driver of relinquishment
Empathy levels are not the key driver of relinquishment
Relinquishers showed markedly lower human-animal empathy
Adopters had significantly higher empathy than relinquishers
mcqs.e: Empathy scores were high in both groups, so a lack of empathy was not identified as the key driver of relinquishment.

mcqs.q: What was found regarding the relationship between human-human and human-animal empathy?
o: A significant link existed between them
The link existed only among relinquishers
mcqs.e: The study reported a significant link between human-human and human-animal empathy.

mcqs.q: How did adopters and relinquishers compare on human-animal empathy?
o: Empathy was not measured in relinquishers
mcqs.e: There were no significant differences in human-animal empathy between adopters and relinquishers.

mcqs.q: What does this case report demonstrate about combining behavioral and medical treatment in a chronically ill homeless dog?
o: Behavioral therapy must wait until medical recovery is complete
Concurrent behavioral and medical treatment was successful
Behavioral therapy worsened the dermatological signs
Medical treatment alone was sufficient for recovery
mcqs.e: Introducing behavioral treatment during medical treatment was challenging but successful and effective.

mcqs.q: Which relationship is specifically outlined in the report?
mcqs.e: The report outlines the relationship between chronic illness and stress.

mcqs.q: Why was evaluating the severity of behavioral disorders difficult in this dog?
o: Only the lack of a known past history
Concurrent dermatological signs such as pain or pruritus complicated assessment
The dog was too young to assess
mcqs.e: Signs of dermatological disease (pain, pruritus) made evaluating behavioral disorder severity very difficult.

mcqs.q: In the Kano model analysis, matching which traits acted as 'Exciters' (unexpected positive features)?
mcqs.e: Matching activity level, affection, and boldness were Kano 'Exciters' for most respondents.

mcqs.q: How was matching to a caretaker's preferred coat color classified?
mcqs.e: Matching to preferred color was an indifferent Kano attribute.

mcqs.q: Matching in affection, activity level, and color was significantly associated with what outcome?
mcqs.e: These matches were significantly associated with dogs being given the maximum satisfaction score.

mcqs.q: Which coat color scored highest for being shy, aloof, and intolerant?
mcqs.e: Gray cats had the highest scores for being shy, aloof, and intolerant.

mcqs.q: Orange cats received the highest scores for which traits?
mcqs.e: Orange cats scored highest for being trainable, friendly, and calm.

mcqs.q: On the Cat Owner Relationship Scale, emotional closeness was positively correlated with which personality profile?
mcqs.e: Emotional closeness correlated positively with active, bold, and friendly personalities.

mcqs.q: What happened to total intake and euthanasia for both dogs and cats over 2016-2020?
mcqs.e: Total intake and euthanasia for both dogs and cats significantly decreased over the study period.

mcqs.q: What was the trend in live release rates across the study period?
mcqs.e: Live release rates for both dogs and cats showed significant increases.

mcqs.q: How did adoption, return-to-owner, and return-to-field as a percentage of intake change?
mcqs.e: Adoption, return-to-owner, return-to-field, and (for cats) transfer all increased significantly as a percentage of intake.

mcqs.q: Which drug classes were the most frequently administered to the shelter cats?
mcqs.e: Antibiotics, antiparasitics, and complementary/protective substances were the most used drugs.

mcqs.q: By active substance, which antibiotics were used most often?
mcqs.e: Penicillins, tetracyclines, and fluoroquinolones were the most-used antibiotics by active substance.

mcqs.q: How did length of stay compare for cats with health records versus those without?
o: It was shorter for cats with records
It was significantly longer for cats with records
mcqs.e: Cats with one or more health records had significantly longer stays than those without.

journal: Journal of Applied Animal Welfare Science

mcqs.q: What was the top decision factor potential adopters considered during shelter visits?
mcqs.e: Dog behavior was the most-considered decision factor (58.9%), significantly greater than chance.

mcqs.q: After behavior, which factors were next most considered?
mcqs.e: Behavior was followed by the dog's age, size, and lifestyle fit.

mcqs.q: Did the set of decision factors differ by adopter age group, household type, or prior pet experience?
o: Yes, it varied strongly by age
It varied only by household type
No, similar sets were considered regardless of group
It varied only by prior pet experience
mcqs.e: Adopters considered similar sets of factors independent of age, household type, or prior experience.

journal: Journal of Applied Animal Welfare Science

mcqs.q: Which factors were significant for the relinquisher group in this Portuguese study?
o: Presence of children and apartment dwelling
mcqs.e: The only significant factors for relinquishers were presence of children and apartment-type dwelling.

mcqs.q: Duration of guardianship before relinquishment was significantly shorter when?
mcqs.e: Guardianship before relinquishment was shorter when children were in the household.

mcqs.q: Which two groups were compared in the survey?
mcqs.e: The study compared relinquishers (REL) with non-relinquishers (NREL).

mcqs.q: How much longer did cats adopted as part of a multi-cat outcome spend on the adoption floor?
mcqs.e: Multi-cat-outcome cats spent about three days (42%) longer on the adoption floor.

mcqs.q: For cats flagged as 'must be adopted together,' how did adoption time differ?
mcqs.e: Cats requiring joint adoption stayed about 13 days (185%) longer.

mcqs.q: What did the study find about shelter-assigned pairs versus behaviorally-defined pairs?
o: A large discrepancy between the two classifications
mcqs.e: There was a large discrepancy between shelter multi-outcome classifications and behavior-based pairings.

mcqs.q: Which factors increased a cat's risk of being returned?
o: Older age at adoption or a bite history
mcqs.e: Cats older at adoption or with a bite history had an increased risk of return.

mcqs.q: Which factor decreased the risk of return?
mcqs.e: Cats in foster care before adoption had a decreased risk of return.

mcqs.q: How did short-term (<30 day) and long-term (>30 day) return reasons differ?
o: Cost and stray dominated short-term returns
Behavior/unwanted/other-pet were short-term; cost/personal/euthanasia/stray were long-term
Reasons were identical in both windows
mcqs.e: Short-term returns were more often for behavior, unwanted, or other pets; long-term for personal reasons, cost, euthanasia, and stray.

mcqs.q: Which confinement practice did Australian dog owners support most strongly?
o: Confining dogs to the owner's property whenever unsupervised (98%)
mcqs.e: Dog owners most strongly supported confining dogs to the property whenever unsupervised (98% agreement).

mcqs.q: Which confinement practice did cat owners support most strongly?
o: Confining cats inside the house at night (89%)
mcqs.e: Cat owners most strongly supported confining cats inside at night (89% agreement).

mcqs.q: Which strategies did the authors recommend to reduce stray animals?
o: Assisting low-income owners with fencing, identification, and free targeted sterilization
mcqs.e: Recommendations included help with fencing, identification, and high-intensity free sterilization targeted to high-impoundment areas.

mcqs.q: What did the study find about health-problem knowledge among people with positive attitudes toward brachycephalic dogs?
o: They had lower knowledge of health problems
They associated more health problems with brachycephalism
They denied any health problems exist
mcqs.e: Contrary to expectations, people with positive attitudes associated more health problems with brachycephalism.

mcqs.q: Did the dogs' tendency to form eye contact explain their popularity?
o: No, eye-contact preference did not play a role
mcqs.e: Eye-contact tendency did not appear to play a role in brachycephalic dogs' popularity.

mcqs.q: What implication did the authors draw for educational campaigns?
o: Factual health knowledge alone is sufficient
Factual knowledge alone is insufficient to reverse the welfare crisis
mcqs.e: Factual knowledge about health problems alone is not enough to reverse the brachycephalic welfare crisis.
